signature.name: Petronas Towers
signature.detail: The twin towers are Kuala Lumpur's defining icon and a symbol of the city's modern skyline. Book the skybridge and observation deck tickets in advance, and go at dusk for day and night views. The towers are easy to reach by LRT at KLCC station.

signature.name: Batu Caves
signature.detail: A massive Hindu shrine set in limestone caves, reached by a steep flight of colorful steps guarded by the giant Lord Murugan Statue. Go early morning to avoid heat and crowds. Dress respectfully, covering shoulders and knees, and take the KTM Komuter train to Batu Caves station.

signature.name: Merdeka Square
signature.detail: This historic square is where Malaysia's independence was declared, surrounded by colonial-era buildings and the tall flagpole. Visit in the cooler early morning and combine it with nearby Masjid Jamek and Central Market on foot.

signature.name: KL Tower
signature.detail: A landmark telecommunications tower with an observation deck offering sweeping views over the city and the Petronas Towers. Come around sunset for the best light. Tickets are sold at the base, and it is a short walk from Bukit Bintang.

signature.name: Thean Hou Temple
signature.detail: One of the largest Chinese temples in Southeast Asia, with ornate roofs and city views from its hillside setting. It is free to enter; dress modestly and visit in the morning for quieter grounds. A taxi or ride-hailing car is the easiest way up.

signature.name: Islamic Arts Museum Malaysia
signature.detail: A world-class museum with beautiful collections of Islamic art, textiles and architecture models, plus a good cafe. It is a calm, air-conditioned break from the heat. Check opening hours, as it closes on some public holidays, and it sits near the National Mosque of Malaysia.

signature.name: Merdeka 118
signature.detail: One of the world's tallest skyscrapers, this new landmark dominates the skyline near Merdeka Square. The observation deck requires timed tickets booked ahead. It is best combined with a walk through the historic Merdeka Square area.

signature.name: National Mosque of Malaysia
signature.detail: A striking modern mosque with a distinctive folded-roof design, open to visitors outside prayer times. Entry is free; dress code requires covered shoulders and legs, with robes often provided. It is a short walk from the Islamic Arts Museum Malaysia.

food: Casual meal $3-8; hawker food at Jalan Alor is cheap
transport: LRT/MRT about $0.50-1 a ride; ride-hailing cars cheap
